val ledger.era.dijkstra.DijkstraUTxO.ins.note: every member of the reference's three instances. The keys needed are Conway's (`getConwayWitsVKeyNeeded`): on the testnet's transactions they are a subset of each level's witnesses, and on the reference's UTXOW cases the keys not witnessed are its recorded missing key; a component check under CNF-2, not the I1 verdict or the resulting state, as an undercomputed set passes the subset check. The minimum fee is Conway's, equal to the reference's recorded minimum of its one `FeeTooSmallUTxO`, a case without redeemers, sub-transactions or reference scripts. Over the batch, the scripts needed less the reference scripts are exactly the witnesses on the testnet's transactions, and the reference's recorded missing and extraneous scripts on its UTXOW cases, with a crafted witness of a needed reference script extraneous, as `babbageMissingScripts` has it. The spending datum is Babbage's, compared on Conway. The flat path has `DijkstraUtxo.minFee`, `TxChecks.neededWitnesses` and `TxChecks.supplementalDatumHashes`, for a transaction without Dijkstra's own fields: no complete Dijkstra batch comparison. The annotated transaction's members are of its Gap (#85's item on Dijkstra's script contexts). The batch's scripts with their contexts are the top level's, then each sub-transaction's, a sub-transaction's collection read only while every one before it was collected, as the reference's `sequence` forces its lazy list; the annotated transaction's members read from their deferred values (`Eval`)
